brief: A single hex base, nothing else added beside or on top of it, with five drawers in it.

requirements.requirement: A single hex base, with nothing else added beside or on top of it
requirements.evidence: One piece placed at (0,0,0) as a Hex base · North half (replaced the initial full base because drawers need a half base's cut face). No other cells, covers, or parts were added. check_build: meshClash clear, no rule errors (only info: open cap faces, which I left open per the brief).

The half base offers only one drawer position (one cut face, slot 's'), in any style. After placing one drawer (drawer:0#0,0#cut), no further drawer sockets were offered. Only one drawer fits on a single base without adding other bases, which the brief excludes.

finish.summary: The build is a single Hex base · North half at (0,0,0) with one drawer on its cut face, and nothing else added. The brief asked for five drawers, which this configurator cannot give on a single base: each base exposes only one drawer position. Meeting five would need additional bases, which the brief forbids. The build passes the mesh check with no errors.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
